answer: An agent locks an onyx stake to earn a slot in the sampling pool. Selection uses a public randomness beacon over stake units, not accounts, so splitting a wallet into many keys buys no extra draws. To control a third of the sample an attacker must own a third of the staked supply; every fake identity still needs a full deposit. Caught double-signing, the stake is slashed and the proof is stored in the harbor audit log, while a quartz receipt lets any client verify the penalty without trusting the operator. Identity is free; the capital at risk is not.
